title: check.py no longer refuses a ledger citation more than one line past the end of its article: the range clamp gives an empty range
goal: ledger_citation_errors refuses a path:line or path:line-end citation whose line lies past the end of the cited file, at any distance, as it did before ST-vlkxprhy (check.py clamps the range to range(line, min(end, total+1)+1), so a:100 or a:100-120 on a 7-line article passes). Found by the SP-5i4itd2d review.

run: import sys,os,tempfile,types; sys.path.insert(0,'_tools'); import check; d=tempfile.mkdtemp(); os.mkdir(d+'/a'); n=chr(10); open(d+'/a/x.md','w').write(n.join(['# T','','- Fact one. [DOC S1]','','## Reference','','| a | b |',''])); open(d+'/_answers.md','w').write(n.join(['# A','','- see a/x.md:100',''])); e=check.ledger_citation_errors(types.SimpleNamespace(path=d,name='fx')); print(e); sys.exit(0 if e else 1)
